issues.headline: NDI 6.4 adds native recording, playback APIs
issues.topline: NDI 6.4 is out with a Recording & Playback API that writes an NDI stream to one MKV (video, multichannel audio, frame-accurate metadata) and plays it back while still recording, plus HEVC 4:4:4 with Intel/NVIDIA GPU acceleration.

items.brief: SDK adds record/playback API, HEVC 4:4:4, Wi-Fi receive buffer, synthesized timecode.
items.spec: Single-file MKV record (video + multichannel audio + metadata), read-while-write; HEVC 4:4:4 HW encode/decode on Intel and NVIDIA GPUs
items.title: NDI 6.4
items.watch: Which switchers, recorders and replay tools (vMix, TriCaster, OBS plugins) ship 6.4 record/playback support first.
items.what: Announced Nov 18: NDI 6.4 adds a Recording & Playback API (record to one MKV with frame-accurate metadata, play back while recording), HEVC 4:4:4 full-chroma encode/decode with GPU acceleration, a configurable Wi-Fi receiver buffer, video-only receive modes at lowest/highest bandwidth, synthesized timecode, clock-drift fixes and a headless NDI Bridge service with API control. Developers can download the updated SDKs now; record/playback monitoring-and-control API keys are on request for NDI Advanced licensees.
items.why: Recording and growing-file playback inside NDI itself means vendors can build ISO record and instant-replay-style tools without a separate capture path; 4:4:4 HEVC keeps graphics and text clean on lower-bitrate links.

issues.headline: EVS confirms cut; XT-S ships early 2027
issues.topline: EVS's Q3 update (Nov 17) confirmed the lowered FY2026 revenue range of EUR 190–205M, gave an EBIT range of only EUR 8–20M, and set first XT-S deliveries, to Game Creek Video and AMP VISUAL TV, for early 2027.

items.brief: FY2026 revenue range EUR 190–205M confirmed; EBIT range EUR 8–20M; no interim dividend.
items.spec: XT-S early adopters: Game Creek Video, AMP VISUAL TV
items.title: EVS Q3 2026 business update
items.watch: XT-S channel counts, ST 2110 support and pricing, and any early-2027 field reports from Game Creek trucks.
items.what: EVS published its Q3 update after market close on Nov 17. It confirmed the FY2026 revenue range it cut on Oct 7 (EUR 190–205M, down from EUR 220–240M) and set FY2026 EBIT at EUR 8.0–20.0M and EBITDA at EUR 26.0–38.0M, citing the lower revenue base, high fixed costs and non-cash write-downs on some intangible assets. There is no interim dividend for 2026. EVS says order intake picked up somewhat after a weak September. First XT-S deliveries, to early adopters Game Creek Video and AMP VISUAL TV, are planned for early 2027.
items.why: Most U.S. trucks run EVS for replay. XT-S is EVS's software-defined successor to the XT server line, so its 2027 timing decides when trucks can move to it. A tighter EVS budget can also affect support headcount and how fast new features ship.

items.what: Haivision announced on Nov 17 that Microsoft chose the Makito ONE video transport platform and Haivision Pro mobile transmitters for a technology refresh. They join Microsoft's existing Makito X4 encoders and decoders and SRT Gateway, bringing its fleet to more than 150 devices. Microsoft runs more than 600 live events a year on the system, including Ignite (Nov 17–20, San Francisco). There it handles contribution, on-site signal routing, overflow rooms and keynote delivery, with Hub 360 as the cloud master control.
items.why: This is a large corporate-event deployment of SRT and bonded cellular for contribution and on-site routing, the same mix many event crews are weighing against fiber and SDI for keynotes and overflow.

items.what: Barco has added Absen to its LED Alliance, the program that pairs third-party LED tiles with Barco's Infinipix image processing. The first product is Absen's KLCOB V3 COB Micro LED series at 0.9, 1.2 and 1.5 mm pitch. It gets 24-bit 'True Dynamic Range' processing, Smart-Calibration of the color gamut and guided setup. The pairing was first reported in early November and covered again Nov 16–17. Neither company has given a ship date.
items.why: Barco is moving from processing only its own LED to processing other makers' panels, which puts Infinipix up against Brompton, Megapixel and NovaStar on control-room and broadcast-set walls. Absen is a common tile in rental and install inventories.

issues.headline: Riot drops JPEG XS for 1 Gbps HEVC
issues.topline: Riot produced the League of Legends Worlds final at Barclays Center mostly from its AWS-hosted Seattle hub, moving contribution from JPEG XS over dual 10 Gbps circuits to Sony NXL-ME80 HEVC at about 1 Gbps. Also today: the first nationwide EAS test since 2023 runs at 2:20 p.m. ET.

items.brief: 91 contribution paths over ~1 Gbps HEVC to Seattle; 41 cameras; venue load-in cut to about a day.
items.spec: Sony NXL-ME80: 3G-SDI/2110 in → 1080 HEVC ~25 Mbps, ~1 frame encode; 200 ms Brooklyn–Seattle round trip; Sony MLS-X1 panel in LA driving a Seattle node; AWS: 121 MediaConnect flows, 8 regions, 511 outputs, 16 MediaLive channels
items.title: LoL Worlds Grand Final: "Contribution 2.0" remote production
items.vendor: Riot Games; Sony; Nevion; AWS; NEP
items.watch: Riot plans 2110-to-the-edge flypacks with SDI mostly removed next year, and phone-based IRL co-streaming at Convergence Fest in Las Vegas in December.
items.what: Riot produced the Worlds final at Barclays Center mostly from its AWS-hosted Remote Broadcast Center in Seattle, with the English TD cutting on a Sony MLS-X1 panel in LA. Contribution moved from JPEG XS over dual 10 Gbps last-mile circuits (which capped at about 30 paths) to 91 active-active HEVC paths on Sony NXL-ME80 edge processors. One leg runs on Riot Direct and the other over the open internet via VPN. The full rollout is 72 outbound and 24 return channels on Nevion.
items.why: This is a working answer to the bandwidth cost of JPEG XS REMI: about a tenth of the circuit with one frame of encode, at the price of 200 ms round trip. Riot also built a 9x16 vertical world feed with no operators from the same data-center feeds, and it grew 1,600% in a year.

items.title: Nationwide EAS test today, 2:20 p.m. ET
items.watch: Form Two deadline Nov 19 at 2:20 p.m. ET; Form Three by Jan 4, 2027.
items.what: FEMA, with the FCC, sends the nationwide EAS test through IPAWS as a CAP message using the NPT code, in English and Spanish. Over-the-air monitoring sources are the backup path. Backup date is Dec 3, 2026.
items.why: If you support a station, cable headend or any facility with an ENDEC, Form Two is due by 2:20 p.m. ET Nov 19, and Form Three by Jan 4, 2027. FEMA's advice is to check the recorded MP3, not just the log line. This follows Sage's Rev 96-2 firmware for the 3644 (covered Nov 8).

items.why: This tracks the ProRes-over-2110-22 work seen with Macnica and MLB (Nov 7). A probe that can also generate signals lets you prove an IPMX or 2110 fabric before the endpoints arrive. No version number or price was given.

issues.headline: Yamaha buys disguise, Vizrt closes Chyron
issues.topline: Two consolidation deals in two days: Vizrt closed its Chyron acquisition on Nov 12, and Yamaha agreed on Nov 13 to buy disguise, with closing expected in December. Both companies say existing products and support stay in place for now.

items.brief: Yamaha buys disguise's parent Butterfly Topco; close expected December 2026, price undisclosed.
items.spec: Covers Designer software, X Series, media servers
items.title: Yamaha to acquire disguise
items.watch: The combined roadmap is due in 2027. Watch for pricing or licensing changes to Designer and the X Series, and for any Yamaha/NEXO audio bundling.
items.what: Yamaha announced Nov 13 that it will buy all shares of Butterfly Topco Limited, disguise's parent company, subject to customary conditions, with closing expected in December 2026. disguise becomes a new division of Yamaha. CEO Fernando Küfer, leadership, reporting lines and contracts stay as they are, and the disguise brand is kept.
items.why: This is the second consolidation in two days, after Vizrt–Chyron. disguise is the default media server on many LED and xR builds, and Yamaha (pro audio) now owns it, which puts it alongside the audio stack for venue and touring sales. In the near term, support contacts and contracts don't change.

items.brief: Deal closed Nov 12; Chyron becomes "A Vizrt Company"; terms undisclosed.
items.spec: PRIME graphics, Paint replay/telestration, virtual placement, VSAR, CAMIO, Click Effects
items.title: Vizrt completes acquisition of Chyron
items.watch: Whether PRIME and Paint keep separate development, and how pricing and support contracts change for existing Chyron sites.
items.what: Vizrt announced on Nov 12 that it has completed the acquisition of Chyron; financial terms were not disclosed. Chyron is rebranded "A Vizrt Company." CEO Mike Truex and CFO Frankie Mignano have stepped down and stay 30 days to support integration.
items.why: Two of the main broadcast graphics vendors are now one company, so PRIME, Paint and CAMIO users face roadmap and support questions alongside Viz Engine and TriCaster. Vizrt says existing Chyron systems and workflows stay supported during integration.

items.title: CrewCom Flex frameless IP intercom
items.watch: Pricing, NMOS/IS-04/05 control support, and interop with Riedel/Clear-Com in mixed rental inventories.
items.what: CrewCom Flex runs wired, wireless and browser-based virtual users on AES67 and SMPTE ST 2110 with ST 2022-7 redundancy. There is no central frame: each panel acts as its own matrix. The CXD-32CF (EtherCon plus dual LC fiber) bridges existing CrewCom wireless systems. It can be deployed locally or cloud-native and is managed with CrewWare 2.0.
items.why: Comms that ride the same 2110/AES67 fabric as video, with no frame to rack, suit IP flypacks and REMI hubs. Browser keypanels can reach remote producers without a separate VoIP gateway. Pliant has not published pricing.

items.what: ROE's LDI booth (2203, 2,000 sq ft) will officially launch Graphite Curve, a curved version of Graphite with OneCurveLock settings from 20° concave to 20° convex. It will also show a new rental platform pitched as a single inventory for indoor and outdoor use, new Vanish Air Rental items, and live demos of its proprietary Sirius LED driver IC. Updated ROE Solo and Omni Tube are also on the stand. Specs for the new rental product haven't been released.
items.why: One flat/curved SKU and one indoor/outdoor tile both cut how much rental inventory you have to carry. An in-house driver IC could change ROE's refresh-rate and low-grey performance relative to Brompton- and Megapixel-processed rivals.

items.watch: Whether mid-tier venues take up 6 mm-class boards as prices fall.
items.what: Michael Silbergleid, writing from Hertz Arena, argues that minor-league boards (10, 12 and 16 mm pitch) fed by HD/3G production make replays hard to read, for example jersey numbers. items.brief: AES67/ST 2110 matrix intercom with distributed processing is now shipping in the US.
items.spec: CKP-16 main panel, CDP-16 desktop panel, CBP-24 4-ch beltpack, Flex Virtual Intercom (4/8/16/36 keys), CXD-32CF 32x32 Dante/AES67 bridge; ST 2022-7
items.title: CrewCom Flex frameless IP intercom
items.watch: Pricing, NMOS/IS-04/05 control support, and interop with Riedel/Clear-Com in mixed rental inventories.
items.what: CrewCom Flex runs wired, wireless and browser-based virtual users on AES67 and SMPTE ST 2110 with ST 2022-7 redundancy. There is no central frame: each panel acts as its own matrix. The CXD-32CF (EtherCon plus dual LC fiber) bridges existing CrewCom wireless systems. It can be deployed locally or cloud-native and is managed with CrewWare 2.0.
items.why: Comms that ride the same 2110/AES67 fabric as video, with no frame to rack, suit IP flypacks and REMI hubs. Browser keypanels can reach remote producers without a separate VoIP gateway. Pliant has not published pricing.

Updated ROE Solo and Omni Tube are also on the stand. Specs for the new rental product haven't been released.
items.why: One flat/curved SKU and one indoor/outdoor tile both cut how much rental inventory you have to carry. An in-house driver IC could change ROE's refresh-rate and low-grey performance relative to Brompton- and Megapixel-processed rivals.

issues.topline: The week's big story was centralization: MLS ran 15 Decision Day matches from one Stamford hub, ESPN, The CW, USA Sports and TNT opened college hoops REMI-first, and NEP made IP flypacks that plug into its hubs available. LED processing stayed quiet; no new Brompton, Megapixel, NovaStar or Analog Way releases surfaced.

items.brief: One Stamford hub runs 15 matches in five hours; all 194 cameras to home-run next season.
items.spec: ~132 in / 132 out feeds; 2 Sony-switched PCRs with Ross OverDrive; Evertz core; 16 AE Live pods (up to 4 Viz Engines each); AT&T GVS transport; <2 s glass-to-graphics
items.title: MLS Productions Stamford hub: Decision Day
items.vendor: MLS / Apple; NEP; Riedel (SimplyLive); Sony; Evertz; Vizrt; AT&T
items.watch: Post-event detail on how Decision Day ran at full load, and the 2027 plan to move every match's cameras and replay to Stamford.
items.what: SVG detailed the MLS Productions hub at WWE Studios in Stamford ahead of Decision Day (Nov 7): 15 matches in about five hours, roughly 250 distinct feeds. REMI matches send venue cameras over AT&T GVS to SimplyLive servers in Stamford, switched by IMG directors in London; onsite matches still use EVS in the trucks. REMI venues get a 53-ft NEP unit with camera ops, a TM and an A1, with no producer, director or TD on site.
items.why: This is a working reference design for centralized, multi-language, multi-feed production at league scale, with software replay and remote directors on a transatlantic link. MLS plans SimplyLive replay in Stamford for all matches and all 194 cameras ingested to the hub next season, which removes EVS from the trucks.

items.spec: REMI Pro 7 TX / Pro 10 TX tiers; typical REMI 2 hard + 2 handheld, 1080p SDR; Level A onsite 6 cams + 3 EVS
items.title: ESPN 2026-27 college basketball: REMI, DreamCatcher, Haivision X4, AWS super-slo-mo trial
items.vendor: ESPN / Evertz / Haivision / Vizrt / EVS / AWS
items.watch: Whether the AWS super-slo-mo trial airs at the Champions Classic (Nov 10) or Players Era (Nov 17–28) in Las Vegas, which runs on GCV Peacock, NEP ND1 and Supershooter 8.
items.what: ESPN will produce more than 1,400 men's games from November to April, with REMI originating from Bristol and Charlotte. Most REMI shows run 1080p SDR with Evertz DreamCatcher as primary replay. Haivision X4 encoders are being added on higher-profile REMI games to send multiple iso camera feeds back for redundancy, Viz Libero telestration is on selected shows, and ESPN is exploring AWS cloud super-slo-mo for marquee games. Level A onsite shows carry six cameras, three EVS, a SpotBox and an XFile.
items.why: The largest single college schedule is now standardized on two REMI tiers with DreamCatcher replay at the hub. The X4 multi-iso move and the cloud HFR replay trial show where centralized replay goes next.

items.brief: IP flypacks under NEP Total Facility Control, linkable to NEP hubs, now offered worldwide.
items.spec: 1080p, HDR, 4K; TFC control; NEP Platform; ties to Dallas Datacenter and South Florida Production Hub
items.title: IP-based flypack production kits
items.watch: Kit names, the hardware switcher and router options, and whether they are ST 2110 or another IP transport.
items.what: NEP Americas added IP-based flypack kits that can run alone, combine with each other, or attach to any NEP facility. They are controlled through NEP Total Facility Control, including the IT and network layer. At one summer 2026 international event, the kits used NEP Platform to run Riedel's SimplyLive for switching, replay and multiviewing.
items.why: This gives you truck-class IP production in a smaller footprint, with a ready path to NEP's hub control rooms. It also suggests software switching and replay are now acceptable on top-tier events. NEP has not published switcher hardware, router or ST 2110 specifics, so ask before you spec one.

items.brief: Fully IP OB truck debuts in Belgium with two PCRs and five EVS servers.
items.spec: Up to 16 CCUs, 2 production control rooms, 5 EVS, diPloy IP, T110 support truck
items.title: Nova 110 IP OB truck
items.watch: Gravity hasn't published the switcher, router or ST 2110 and NMOS details.
items.what: Gravity Media's Nova 110 made its debut at the UEFA Europa League match Union Saint-Gilloise vs Real Sociedad in Leuven. It's a fully IP truck that runs on Gravity's diPloy platform. It supports up to 16 camera CCUs, has two production control rooms and five EVS replay systems, and works alongside the T110 equipment truck over fiber and power distribution.
items.why: A second PCR in a mid-size, 16-camera truck lets one IP core serve two productions or a world feed and a unilateral feed. diPloy is the same managed network Gravity used for the IMF/World Bank build in Bangkok.

items.brief: 80x40 K-Frame IP switcher with Kayenne panel and four Kaleido-IP X440 multiviewers.
items.spec: K-Frame 80x40 (IP), Kayenne surface, 4x Kaleido-IP X440
items.title: Franceinfo moves from SDI to ST 2110
items.vendor: France Télévisions / Grass Valley / Red Bee Media France
items.watch: Whether France Télévisions extends 2110 to other channels, and which network core it chose (not disclosed).
items.what: France Télévisions has moved Franceinfo's production from SDI to SMPTE ST 2110 on a fully IP Grass Valley K-Frame (80x40) with a Kayenne control surface and four Kaleido-IP X440 multiviewers. Red Bee Media France integrated it. It went on air Aug 31 for the channel's 10th anniversary; details were published Nov 2.
items.why: This is another reference for running a native-IP K-Frame in a 24/7 news environment, which helps anyone sizing a K-Frame IP and Kaleido-IP build.

items.brief: AMPP video and SSL Virtual Tempest Engine on COTS servers onsite, operated from Ripley.
items.spec: SSL System T VTE; S400 32-fader surface remote; SB 8.8 stagebox; Net I/O ST 2110 Bridge; ~50 Mbps upload over public internet
items.title: Software-defined edge production PoC at BTCC Thruxton
items.vendor: Cloudbass / Solid State Logic / Grass Valley
items.watch: SSL and Cloudbass TD Michael Beaumont present the results at the SVG Europe Sports Audio Summit, Nov 12, Kings Place, London.
items.what: During British Touring Car Championship coverage at Thruxton, Cloudbass ran video (Grass Valley AMPP) and audio (SSL System T Virtual Tempest Engine) on COTS servers at the track. Operators in Cloudbass's Ripley gallery controlled them using about 50 Mbps of upload over a public internet link, carrying control plus monitoring. Full-quality signals stayed onsite. An SSL Net I/O ST 2110 Bridge tied the VTE into the truck's 2110 fabric.
items.why: This is the distributed alternative to centralized REMI: processing stays at the venue, so you don't need multi-gig contribution and latency stays low. Cloudbass estimates the kit could eventually fit in a Sprinter-sized van.

items.brief: First ProRes-over-ST 2110-22 implementation carried 8K stereo live baseball to Vision Pro.
items.spec: 100GbE PCIe Gen4; Altera Agilex-7 FPGA; ST 2110-20/22/30/40/41, ST 2059 PTP, 2022-7, 2110-21; macOS (Thunderbolt chassis + Mac Studio) and Linux
items.title: MEP100 SmartNIC: ProRes over ST 2110-22 for live MLB in Apple Immersive
items.watch: Whether the ProRes-over-2110-22 mapping is submitted to SMPTE or VSF, and MEP100 pricing.
items.what: Macnica says its MEP100 SmartNIC carried ProRes over ST 2110-22 for four live MLB games in Apple Immersive (first was Red Sox at Yankees, Aug 28), with ST 2110-30 spatial audio and lens geometry and distortion maps as a separate ST 2110-41 metadata flow, all PTP-locked over 100GbE.
items.why: It puts a Mac Studio directly on a 2110 fabric with hardware PTP and pacing, and shows 2110-41 carrying production metadata, not only ancillary data. Useful if you are weighing Mac-based tools or immersive formats on an IP plant. The ProRes packetization was not previously published, so treat interoperability with other 2110-22 gear as unproven.

items.brief: OBS is testing cloud, virtualised and AI workflows at Dakar 2026, aimed at LA28.
items.spec: 3 virtualised OB vans across 3 venues at Milano Cortina 2026
items.title: OBS tech cycle: virtualised OB vans, MXL, IP mics toward LA28
items.watch: Dakar post-event reports and any vendors named for OBS's virtualised or MXL work.
items.what: OBS is using the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games (Oct 31 to Nov 13) to judge whether cloud, remote, virtualised and AI workflows should be used. Its audio manager names the next phase as "virtualised production environments, AI-powered tools, cloud-based workflows, MXL technologies, and IP microphones." The virtual OB van, developed since Beijing 2022, ran at three venues at Milano Cortina.
items.why: OBS naming MXL publicly is a sign that the shared-memory exchange for software media functions is on the roadmap of the largest host broadcaster. That should push vendors to support MXL in their software switchers and processors.

items.brief: AIMS chair says 48 products certified at the first IPMX test event and 14 at the second.
items.title: IPMX certification tally: 62 products
items.watch: The date of the next IPMX testing event and a public list of certified products.
items.what: In an AVNetwork piece, AIMS chairman Steve Reynolds (CEO of Imagine Communications) says IPMX became fully certifiable in 2026. He counts 48 products certified at the first formal testing event and 14 more at the second, plus a new IPMX training program.
items.why: Independent certification gives you something firmer than vendor claims for building IPMX into an RFP for venue AV-over-IP that has to connect to ST 2110 broadcast systems.

items.brief: Mexico City studios anchored by a 1.8 mm LED wall of about 26.6M pixels; capacity for 10 simultaneous events.
items.spec: 97 sq m 1.8 mm LED wall, 4x Sony HDC-3500 per studio, EVS Neuron routing
items.title: FOX LATAM Mexico City production hub
items.watch: Watch for the LED and processor vendor and the third studio's spec when it opens in January.
items.what: FOX LATAM runs two studios in Mexico City, and a third is due in January. The newest covers about 200 sq m and is modeled on FOX Sports' LA studios. It's built around a 97 sq m, 1.8 mm-pitch LED wall of nearly 26.6 million pixels, which SVG calls the largest in Latin America. Each studio has four Sony HDC-3500 cameras, and an EVS Neuron handles routing. The site can produce 10 events at once and produced all 104 World Cup matches for Central America across 16 production cells.
items.why: At roughly 26.6M pixels, the wall's canvas is several times the size of a single 4K raster, so it sits in multi-processor, multi-output processing territory. The build is also a reference for running one hub's cells across a regional rights portfolio.

items.brief: UK touring supplier Universal Pixels buys 250 m² of ROE's transparent Vanish Air Rental panels.
items.spec: Power routed through panel frame (no central PSU column); perforated LED layout; custom locks
items.title: Vanish Air Rental: 250 m² for Universal Pixels
items.watch: Pitch, processing and per-panel weight in the first Universal Pixels tour deployment.
items.what: Universal Pixels, a UK live-event and touring supplier, bought 250 m² of ROE Visual Vanish Air Rental transparent LED. ROE says the screen nearly disappears from view at 5–8 m. Universal Pixels' technical head Gareth Manicom cited the light weight and transparency, which allow more complex stage designs without a heavy grid. New this week; AED's European VAR buy was covered Nov 4.
items.why: Two major rental houses adding VAR in one week means transparent outdoor-rated mesh is becoming standard rental stock in Europe and the UK, so it will start showing up in tour and festival designs you have to process and rig.

items.brief: Dual 25GbE SFP28 fiber adapter for Thunderbolt 5 laptops and desktops, shipping now.
items.spec: 2x 25GBASE-SR SFP28 (LC fiber, up to 100 m, transceivers included); TB5 passthrough for 6K display; Mac/Windows/Linux
items.title: Twin25G T5 Thunderbolt 5 adapter
items.watch: Whether any vendor qualifies it for NDI High Bandwidth or software 2110 receivers.
items.what: Sonnet released the Twin25G T5, a Thunderbolt 5 adapter with two 25GbE SFP28 ports and a downstream Thunderbolt 5 port that runs a display up to 6K without cutting Ethernet throughput. It costs $999.99 with two SR transceivers included and is available through Sonnet and resellers as of Nov 4.
items.why: Two 25G fiber ports on a laptop give you a practical path for Mac or PC laptops onto NDI or high-bandwidth file/IP networks in flypacks and edit positions. Sonnet doesn't claim ST 2110 or PTP hardware support, so don't treat it as a 2110 NIC.

items.title: Datapath brand retired, portfolio moves to VITEC
items.watch: Whether warranty terms, part numbers or the roadmap change once the brands combine.
items.what: VITEC says the Datapath corporate brand will be retired and its products will carry the VITEC brand, with the transition running into 2027. Individual product names stay the same, support continues through VITEC, and existing Datapath offices stay open. A combined VITEC website comes later.
items.why: If you spec or own Datapath wall controllers or capture cards, expect new branding on quotes, docs and support portals, but the product names stay. Check that support contacts and firmware download locations don't break during the move.

items.brief: Mandatory, free security update removes weak eMudhra root certificates; must be installed by hand.
items.spec: Model 3644, U.S. units on Rev96 or Rev96-1
items.title: Digital ENDEC 3644 firmware Rev 96-2
items.watch: Sage gave no deadline. Confirm that every 3644 in your plant reports Rev 96-2.
items.what: Sage released Rev 96-2 for the U.S. Digital ENDEC 3644. It removes several eMudhra root certificates whose weak private keys could, in the right circumstances, be used to spoof the domains of the TLS-secured alert audio servers. It also fixes SMTP attachment problems with some mail servers and allows '&' and '+' in web GUI passwords. The ENDEC does not update itself.
items.why: FCC rules require prompt installation of EAS security updates. Any station or facility you support that runs a 3644 needs someone to install this by hand.

items.what: For the first year of a five-year deal running to 2030, Limitless produced Henley fully remote. The site has no internet, so Neutral Wireless installed a private 5G network to carry onboard camera feeds from the umpires' launches and boats, plus a new live timing system.

items.brief: Mandatory, free security update removes weak eMudhra root certificates; must be installed by hand.
items.spec: Model 3644, U.S. units on Rev96 or Rev96-1
items.title: Digital ENDEC 3644 firmware Rev 96-2
items.watch: Sage gave no deadline. Confirm that every 3644 in your plant reports Rev 96-2.
items.what: Sage released Rev 96-2 for the U.S. Digital ENDEC 3644. It removes several eMudhra root certificates whose weak private keys could, in the right circumstances, be used to spoof the domains of the TLS-secured alert audio servers. It also fixes SMTP attachment problems with some mail servers and allows '&' and '+' in web GUI passwords. The ENDEC does not update itself.
items.why: FCC rules require prompt installation of EAS security updates. Any station or facility you support that runs a 3644 needs someone to install this by hand.

items.why: Multi Matrix makes Cinema EOS bodies easier to intercut with system cameras in a shaded show. One free controller for a mixed Canon PTZ and cinema fleet saves you building a separate control setup. Canon has not given firmware version numbers.

issues.headline: Gravity rolls IP truck; FOX LATAM's LED hub
issues.topline: Gravity Media put its fully IP Nova 110 OB truck on air in Belgium with five EVS servers and two production control rooms. FOX LATAM also detailed a Mexico City hub built around a 97 sq m, 1.8 mm LED wall that can produce 10 events at once.

items.brief: Fully IP OB truck debuts in Belgium with two PCRs and five EVS servers.
items.spec: Up to 16 CCUs, 2 production control rooms, 5 EVS, diPloy IP, T110 support truck
items.title: Nova 110 IP OB truck
items.watch: Gravity hasn't published the switcher, router or ST 2110 and NMOS details.
items.what: Gravity Media's Nova 110 made its debut at the UEFA Europa League match Union Saint-Gilloise vs Real Sociedad in Leuven. It's a fully IP truck that runs on Gravity's diPloy platform. It supports up to 16 camera CCUs, has two production control rooms and five EVS replay systems, and works alongside the T110 equipment truck over fiber and power distribution.
items.why: A second PCR in a mid-size, 16-camera truck lets one IP core serve two productions or a world feed and a unilateral feed. diPloy is the same managed network Gravity used for the IMF/World Bank build in Bangkok.

items.brief: Mexico City studios anchored by a 1.8 mm LED wall of about 26.6M pixels; capacity for 10 simultaneous events.
items.spec: 97 sq m 1.8 mm LED wall, 4x Sony HDC-3500 per studio, EVS Neuron routing
items.title: FOX LATAM Mexico City production hub
items.watch: Watch for the LED and processor vendor and the third studio's spec when it opens in January.
items.what: FOX LATAM runs two studios in Mexico City, and a third is due in January. The newest covers about 200 sq m and is modeled on FOX Sports' LA studios. It's built around a 97 sq m, 1.8 mm-pitch LED wall of nearly 26.6 million pixels, which SVG calls the largest in Latin America. Each studio has four Sony HDC-3500 cameras, and an EVS Neuron handles routing. The site can produce 10 events at once and produced all 104 World Cup matches for Central America across 16 production cells.
items.why: At roughly 26.6M pixels, the wall's canvas is several times the size of a single 4K raster, so it sits in multi-processor, multi-output processing territory. The build is also a reference for running one hub's cells across a regional rights portfolio.

items.brief: Corporate summit run like a sports host broadcast: 75 recording channels, ST 2110, 160 Bolero beltpacks.
items.spec: 45 rooms (21 to MCR), 75 recording channels, EVS + X_File, 10 edit stations, 45 intercom panels
items.title: IMF/World Bank Annual Meetings host production
items.watch: See whether this centralized-MCR model spreads to other multi-room summits and conferences.
items.what: Gravity Media ran the Oct 12–18 IMF and World Bank Annual Meetings at Bangkok's Queen Sirikit National Convention Centre. The design used red/blue diPloy networks on dark fiber with ST 2110 and orchestration, a central MCR with streaming outputs, and dedicated VLANs for Zoom, Webex and Teams. The build covered 75 centralized EVS/X_File recording channels, 10 edit stations, 160 Riedel Bolero beltpacks on 45 antennas, and more than 50 interpretation systems.
items.why: It's a concrete template for large corporate and government events: a centralized 2110 recording core, red/blue redundancy and UC-platform VLANs instead of room-by-room AV islands.

items.spec: VAR: 92% transparency, power through frame (no center PSU column); Topaz 1.9: concave/convex curve
items.title: Vanish Air Rental and Topaz 1.9 rental buy
items.watch: Check processor pairing and VAR pixel pitch and brightness before you spec it. The article gives neither.
items.what: AED Group bought ROE Visual Vanish Air Rental (VAR) and Topaz 1.9 panels. VAR is an outdoor transparent panel. Its thin frame carries power, which removes the central power-supply column, and ROE rates its transparency at 92%. Topaz 1.9 curves both concave and convex. AED plans to feature it at its WHEREAS event at Barcelona Fair in February 2027.
items.why: A major rental house stocking VAR makes it easier to spec transparent touring and festival LED in continental Europe without a custom buy.

items.spec: 160 MHz (3.98–4.14 GHz) to auction; statutory close July 2027
items.title: Upper C-band repack and backhaul planning
items.watch: Watch for the FCC auction procedures notice and earth station transition deadlines.
items.what: In an SVG interview, Sinclair's Paul Spinelli covers how next summer's C-band repack affects the company's transmission and backhaul strategy, including for Tennis Channel. The FCC's July 22 order set up an auction of 160 MHz of upper C-band (3.98–4.14 GHz), due to close by July 2027. Winning bidders can light up service in December 2030 in the top 75 markets.
items.why: Anyone who still relies on C-band for sports contribution or as a fiber backup should budget now for Ku-band, terrestrial IP, LEO or hybrid paths, and track which costs are reimbursable.

issues.headline: College hoops goes REMI-first; edge PoC at Thruxton
issues.topline: ESPN will produce 1,400+ college basketball games this season, most as REMI from Bristol and Charlotte on Evertz DreamCatcher, adding Haivision X4 encoders for iso feeds and trialing AWS cloud super-slo-mo. Cloudbass separately proved an edge-compute model: AMPP plus SSL's virtual Tempest engine onsite, controlled over ~50 Mbps of public internet.

items.what: ESPN will produce more than 1,400 men's games from November to April, with REMI originating from Bristol and Charlotte. Most REMI shows run 1080p SDR with Evertz DreamCatcher as primary replay. Haivision X4 encoders are being added on higher-profile REMI games to send multiple iso camera feeds back for redundancy, Viz Libero telestration is on selected shows, and ESPN is exploring AWS cloud super-slo-mo for marquee games. Level A onsite shows carry six cameras, three EVS, a SpotBox and an XFile.
items.why: The largest single college schedule is now standardized on two REMI tiers with DreamCatcher replay at the hub. The X4 multi-iso move and the cloud HFR replay trial show where centralized replay goes next.

items.vendor: Cloudbass / Solid State Logic / Grass Valley
items.watch: SSL and Cloudbass TD Michael Beaumont present the results at the SVG Europe Sports Audio Summit, Nov 12, Kings Place, London.
items.what: During British Touring Car Championship coverage at Thruxton, Cloudbass ran video (Grass Valley AMPP) and audio (SSL System T Virtual Tempest Engine) on COTS servers at the track. Operators in Cloudbass's Ripley gallery controlled them using about 50 Mbps of upload over a public internet link, carrying control plus monitoring. Full-quality signals stayed onsite. An SSL Net I/O ST 2110 Bridge tied the VTE into the truck's 2110 fabric.
items.why: This is the distributed alternative to centralized REMI: processing stays at the venue, so you don't need multi-gig contribution and latency stays low. Cloudbass estimates the kit could eventually fit in a Sprinter-sized van.

items.what: Blackmagic launched UltraStudio Express HD, its first UltraStudio on USB4/Thunderbolt 4. It supports SD and HD up to 1080p60 and works with the DeckLink API and Desktop Video SDK.
items.why: It's a cheap laptop-based way to add fill/key playback, ingest or a deck-controlled capture station for a flypack or graphics position. Published prices differ between outlets, so check the reseller quote, especially after Blackmagic's Oct 20 price increase.

issues.headline: Blackmagic reprices 2110; IPMX edge gear ships
issues.topline: Blackmagic's Oct 20 price increase on 36 products (2110 converters up as much as ~80%) and its new $2,525 100G Ethernet Switch 820 reset the low-cost ST 2110 math for bids. Also this week: patch PHP2Shell on any device web UI, and an IPMX/2110 dual-mode transceiver from PlexusAV is now shipping.

items.brief: Prices rise up to ~80% (2110 IP SDI to HDMI 12G $515→$925) on ATEM, HyperDeck, 2110 converters and Cloud Store; cameras unchanged.
items.price: ATEM 4 M/E Constellation IP Plus now $19,960
items.spec: ATEM 4 M/E Constellation IP Plus $12,995→$19,960; ATEM 4 M/E Constellation IP $7,995→$10,845; ATEM Mini Extreme ISO G2 $1,995→$3,090; HyperDeck ISO Recorder 100G $4,995→$6,035; 2110 IP Converter 8x12G SFP $2,665→$3,575
items.title: Price increase on 36 products (ATEM, HyperDeck, 2110 IP)
items.watch: Whether other vendors with memory-heavy hardware (servers, recorders, storage) follow with their own increases.
items.what: Blackmagic raised reseller prices worldwide on 36 products (USD list), effective immediately for new orders. Backorders ship at the old price. Covered lines include ATEM switchers, HyperDecks, the 2110 IP converter range, DeckLink IP, StudioBridge 100G, Cloud Store and Videohub Mini. Cameras and accessories are not affected in this round.
items.why: Blackmagic is the low-cost entry point for ST 2110 and ISO-recording builds; the 2110 line took some of the largest increases, which changes the cost gap against Ross, AJA and others on bids. Quotes or budgets built before Oct 20 are now short.

items.brief: 100G switch built for ST 2110, with redundant PTP clock ports, at $2,525.

items.title: Ethernet Switch 820
items.watch: Whether it gets NMOS or a third-party broadcast controller integration, and whether the price holds after Blackmagic's Oct 20 increase on 36 products.
items.what: Blackmagic released the Ethernet Switch 820: eight 100G QSFP ports, two 10G ports, two redundant PTP clock ports (two separate grandmasters can be attached), isolated 1G management and redundant power. It is managed with the free Blackmagic Ethernet Utility on macOS and Windows.
items.why: It rounds out Blackmagic's 100G 2110 stack (ATEM, HyperDeck and converters) with its own fabric at a price far below typical broadcast spine/leaf switches. For small flypacks or a single control room it could replace a COTS switch plus PTP config work. Check it against your NMOS/SDN control and multicast scale before planning around it.

items.brief: Critical PHP remote-code flaws; any gear with a PHP web management UI may be exposed.
items.spec: CVSS v3 9.8 (Fortinet rating); fixed in PHP 8.5.12 / 8.4.27 / 8.3.36 / 8.2.35
items.title: PHP2Shell vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619)
items.vendor: PHP Foundation; Palo Alto Networks, Cisco, Fortinet advisories
items.watch: Palo Alto's remaining PAN-OS fixes were due Oct 27–30; check codec, processor and intercom vendors' bulletins this week.
items.what: PHP released security fixes on Oct 21 for two critical flaws that can let an unauthenticated attacker run code on a web server. TV Tech's Oct 26 guidance warns that audio processors, codecs, transmitters and other devices with browser management portals may embed PHP. PAN-OS management UIs are affected, with more Palo Alto fixes due Oct 27–30; Cisco has Expressway, URWB and Duo Access Gateway vulnerable and Catalyst 1300 switches under investigation.
items.why: Encoders, LED/AV processors, intercom and IP gateways on show networks often expose web UIs, and PHP 8.1 and older get no upstream fix. Vendors, not you, have to ship firmware for embedded devices.

items.brief: Five Tessera SX40s and 20 XD 10G units drive a 10,752×2,816 main wall.

items.vendor: Brompton Technology, INFiLED, Production Video Group, Disguise
items.watch: Whether Tessera 3.6 moves out of beta before LDI (Dec 6–8).
items.what: Brompton published (Oct 28) the processing design for Bad Bunny's stadium tour. Four 4K Tessera SX40s each feed four XD 10G units for the main upstage wall, and one SX40 with four XD units drives the two delay screens. Each main-wall panel run uses two XD units for closed-loop cable redundancy. The system runs 10-bit end to end with custom LUTs, fed by four standard UHD outputs from Disguise GX 3+ servers.
items.why: It's a current reference for splitting a very wide stadium canvas across standard UHD server outputs instead of custom rasters. Note the redundancy is at the cable/XD level only; there is no processor redundancy in this design.

items.brief: Two Tessera SX40s and an S8 drive 1,000+ sq ft of LG LED with Frame Remapping.
items.spec: 2× Tessera SX40 (wall) with 4× XD 10G; 1× Tessera S8 (ceiling); Mo-Sys tracking; up to 60fps, path to 120fps
items.title: VG Media Studio virtual production stage on Tessera
items.watch: Whether Tessera 3.6 (now in BETA 1) moves to stable; 3.5.2 remains the current stable release.
items.what: VG Media Studio in Laichingen, Germany, runs more than 1,000 sq ft of LG LED in front of a roughly 2,690 sq ft stage. Two 4K Tessera SX40 processors, each feeding two XD 10G distribution boxes, drive the wall, and a Tessera S8 drives the ceiling. The stage uses Frame Remapping to give individual cameras different feeds, along with Custom Markers, hidden tracking markers and Stream Deck control.
items.why: It's a mid-size reference build for multi-camera LED stages: Frame Remapping lets each camera see its own background without a second wall. Note that 120fps needs further configuration on this setup.

items.what: PlexusAV made the P-AVN-6-S available globally through resellers on Oct 30. It handles uncompressed video up to 4K60 over ST 2110 or IPMX and JPEG XS on the same unit, with no extra licences for either mode. It was certified at the August IPMX testing event in Geneva. Price not published.
items.why: One box that speaks both 2110 and IPMX, with PTP-to-genlock and SDI, is the kind of edge device that lets an event or venue system bridge broadcast trucks and ProAV IP without separate gateways.

The platform is sized for almost 60 services, and about 40 more linear services, including live-source channels, are being assessed. Cloud disaster recovery is being explored.
items.why: It's a large software-defined playout deployment that stays on-prem with ST 2022-2 rather than ST 2110 or public cloud. That's a pragmatic model for facilities migrating gradually.

items.watch: Whether the league names its cloud stack and adds more clubs or builds its own studio hub for 2027-28.
items.what: NHL Productions is producing local broadcasts for the Ducks, Hurricanes, Blue Jackets, Stars, Wild and Blues. Each home market gets a Mobile TV Group FLEX/HDX truck (44FLEX, 29HDX, 52FLEX, 38FLEX, 54FLEX, 45FLEX). Road games run from cloud control rooms located in-arena (Carolina, Columbus, St. Louis), at studios (Dallas, Minnesota) or offsite (Anaheim). Gameday Creative built a hub-and-spoke graphics system shared by all six, and the league plans its own studio hub; NHL Network's Secaucus facility serves as the base this season.
items.why: It's a working template for one producer running many regional feeds on a standard camera plot, shared graphics and cloud road-game control. That model applies to any team or league consolidating regional production. SVG doesn't name the switcher, replay, cloud platform or transport vendors.

Alpha Video was lead integrator with Unity Systems Integration; Anthony James Partners consulted on design. Models and manufacturers were not disclosed.

issues.headline: Prime Video puts virtual replay in AWS
issues.topline: Prime Video opened its second NBA season with Prime 360, an AI virtual-camera replay system that reconstructs plays in 3D on AWS from a calibrated camera ring around the court. SVG's World Series follow-up also filled in FOX's truck plan and first-ever dirtcams.

items.brief: AI virtual camera rebuilds NBA plays in 3D on AWS for replay and analysis.
items.spec: Perimeter array of synced, calibrated cameras; AWS Trainium; trucks on 400G Lawo/Arista ST 2110
items.title: Prime 360 virtual camera system
items.vendor: Prime Video, AWS, Game Creek Video
items.watch: Whether Prime publishes camera count, round-trip latency or a turnaround time per clip.
items.what: Prime 360 uses a ring of calibrated, synchronized high-resolution cameras around the court. The footage goes to AWS, where proprietary AI models running on Trainium chips reconstruct the play in 3D. Operators rotate the virtual camera and set keyframes like editing a clip. It is used in-game and in pre/half/postgame on select broadcasts. SVG gives no camera count or latency figure. The show itself is native 1080p HDR from Game Creek's Bird and Magic (up to 16 Sony HDC-5500 plus 16 more over ST 2110 each) and the Encore studio unit.
items.why: This is volumetric replay running as a cloud service in a tier-one live show rather than as an on-site server. It's a sign that some 'replay' angles will come from compute and contribution bandwidth, not another hard camera or EVS channel.

items.what: SVG adds what TV Tech's camera list left out. Game Creek Yogi handles Milwaukee, with two compounds about 500 ft apart linked by fiber. NEP ND1 moved from Los Angeles to Tropicana Field. Fletcher supplies three wireless dirtcams buried at home plate and the mound, a World Series first, received with high-gain antennas aimed down. A Rush Media truck carries the FOX Sports Latin America feed for FOX Mexico and FOX Deportes, also a first. Bolt 6 runs the AR. Vendors include BSI, Bexel and CES Power. Replay server and HDR details still aren't published.
items.why: Buried wireless cameras and a separate-language truck are both RF and compound-planning problems as much as camera ones. The 55-second goalpost lighting truss (four crew vs. ~8 minutes and eight crew for a roof) is also a useful changeover reference for concourse sets.

items.brief: Self-service Linux-container ZoomISO Cloud instances inside CLOUDflex, with NDI out per participant.
items.price: CLOUDflex hourly hosting fee; customer supplies Zoom license

Customers use their own Zoom Enhanced Media Add-On or Zoom Events Hub Host seat. CLOUDflex bills hosting only for the hours the instance runs. It was previewed at IBC 2026.
items.why: Remote guest ISOs are a routine need on corporate and hybrid events. Hourly cloud instances avoid holding an on-prem ZoomISO machine for occasional shows, though NDI-only output means planning your own SRT or 2110 handoff.

items.brief: NFL's Green-GO coach-to-coach and medical comms now ride 5G bridges, same kits abroad.

items.what: Green-GO (distributed in the U.S. by Nova Lume) runs the NFL's coach-to-coach, officiating and Video Injury Review System comms. The system moved to Verizon 5G via Green-GO bridges, with 4G support domestically. Each team travels with about 78 wired and wireless packs, so international games use the same kit as home games. Each sideline cart is redundant, with two Surface laptops and four radios. Coach-to-player helmet audio cuts at 15 seconds on the 40-second clock.
items.why: It shows a mission-critical intercom running over cellular bridges rather than dedicated RF or fiber. That's a model worth noting for touring and pop-up venues where you don't own the network.

items.title: 2026 World Series production

items.title: Professional Services expanded to AV-over-IP, starting with NDI
items.watch: Which partner protocol comes next. NETGEAR says it stays protocol-neutral, so Dante, IPMX or ST 2110 are all possible.
items.what: NETGEAR extended its Professional Services program from network design to AV-over-IP workflows, with NDI as the first ecosystem partner. Engagements are project-based, separate from Premium Support tiers, and sold through NETGEAR's two-tier channel. No pricing was disclosed, and no new products were announced.
items.why: NDI systems usually fail at the network: multicast, QoS and switch profiles. One vendor taking responsibility for both the switch config and the NDI design can reduce finger-pointing on integrator-built venue systems.

issues.headline: Quiet day
issues.topline: Quiet day after NAB Show New York closed with no new pricing or ship dates; the useful reads are ESPN's native-HDR NBA build and FOX's World Cup IP transport lessons.

items.brief: ESPN opens its NBA season in 1080p HDR, with native-HDR GCV trucks and new remote control rooms.
items.spec: 1080p HDR; Sony HDC-5500; 5–11 manned cameras; REMI replay ratio 1:4 on-site:remote
items.title: NBA on ESPN: native-HDR trucks and Bristol PCRs
items.vendor: ESPN, Game Creek Video, SMT, NEP Specialty Capture, EVS, AWS
items.watch: Whether at-home EVS replay goes from test to regular use on NBA or MNF games this season.
items.what: Every Game Creek Video truck on ESPN's NBA package now has native HDR infrastructure, led by Flagship and Gridiron. New native-HDR PCRs in Bristol cut down on on-site cross-conversion. Bristol and Charlotte PCRs support nearly all games. For REMI games, virtual ads and shot-distance graphics move from a downstream Bristol device to on-site insertion on the Camera 1 chain (SMT). ESPN uses AWS-based super-slow-motion tools and has tested at-home EVS replay operators with GCV.
items.why: It confirms 1080p HDR as the default spec for top-tier live sports, with ESPN, NBC and Prime Video all moving the same way. It also shows where REMI is going: graphics insertion moves back to the venue, while replay and super-slo-mo move off site.

items.brief: Transmission leads cover FOX's World Cup IP backbone, C-band repurposing, NBC's LEO contribution and MoQ.
items.title: SVG TranSPORT: FOX World Cup IP network, C-band, LEO, MoQ
items.vendor: FOX Sports, NBC Sports, Paramount/CBS, SES, Cobalt Digital, PSSI
items.watch: FCC auction timing and relocation-fund details for C-band earth stations, which the session did not pin to dates.
items.what: At SVG TranSPORT (Oct 20, NYC), FOX described the new IP network it built for the 2026 FIFA World Cup. It linked the Dallas IBC, FOX Network Center in LA, the Tempe tech center, a New York backup studio and venue BRISK kits, and automated failover kept coverage on air through repeated circuit failures. Panels covered the FCC plan to repurpose 160 MHz of C-band for 5G, and NBC Sports/NBC Olympics described their LEO satellite contribution work. Cobalt's Ciro Noronha proposed Ku-band plus RIST over public internet to cover rain fade, and Media over QUIC was pitched for sub-second contribution and distribution.
items.why: C-band loss changes how you plan backhaul for remote shoots: you'll need Ku, LEO, fiber or internet paths with automated failover, and those need to be in the budget and in the redundancy design now.

items.brief: Partnership validates Visionary 5 Series AV-over-IP endpoints in and out of CALICO PRO processor.
items.spec: 4K over 1GbE (tested configs); HDMI in/out via CALICO PRO modules
items.title: Visionary 5 Series + tvONE CALICO PRO interoperability
items.watch: Whether either vendor publishes the tested resolution/frame-rate matrix or adds IPMX support.
items.what: Visionary 5 Series decoders feed HDMI into CALICO PRO inputs, and CALICO PRO outputs feed 5 Series encoders back onto the network to remote displays. tvONE engineers tested resolutions, frame rates, EDID and image quality across the configurations they tried. The release doesn't mention IPMX.
items.why: It's a vendor-tested path for central wall processing with sources and displays spread across a 1GbE AV-over-IP network, so control rooms and fixed installs can use one processor instead of local scalers.

issues.headline: Two campus builds split on SDI vs. IP
issues.topline: Two new college builds went different ways: the University of Washington put four control rooms on ST 2110 with Grass Valley K-Frame SXP. Northwestern's new Ryan Field opened on 3G-SDI baseband with IP-ready hybrid gear. NAB Show New York's first day brought small product news, not major launches.

items.brief: UW runs four control rooms off two K-Frame SXP IP frames on ST 2110.
items.spec: 2× K-Frame SXP (128 IP in / 64 IP out each), 2× Kayenne + 2× Karrera 3 M/E, 10 LDX, ST 2022-7, 12G UHD/HDR
items.title: Sundodger Studios four-control-room ST 2110 facility
items.vendor: Grass Valley, CTI, Anthony James Partners
items.watch: Planned integration with Daktronics systems at UW's athletics venues.
items.what: The University of Washington replaced a smaller SDI system with four ST 2110 control rooms. They run on two K-Frame SXP frames, each shared by two rooms. Cameras are 4× LDX 135, 4× LDX 150 (3x/6x), and 2× wireless LDX 135 on XCU Xpress UXF bases. Shading is through Creative Grading panels and a CCS-ONE server. CTI integrated the facility and AJP designed it.
items.why: Running two control rooms per K-Frame SXP, with Kayenne and Karrera panels mixed, is a cost-sharing model worth noting for multi-room college or venue builds.

items.brief: 11 SNA displays (32.1M pixels) driven by Ross Tessera/Carbonite; control room launched on 3G-SDI.
items.spec: End zones 3,840×1,740 at 8 mm; 10 mm ribbons, 2,500+ ft; Great Hall 1.2 mm 5,760×2,160; K-Frame 3M/E Kayenne, Evertz NEXX + DreamCatcher
items.title: New Ryan Field video and LED systems
items.vendor: SNA Displays, Ross Video, Grass Valley, Evertz, Anthony James Partners
items.watch: Whether the IP upgrade arrives within the stated one-to-two-year window.
items.what: Northwestern's $875M, 35,000-seat stadium has 16,250 sq ft of SNA LED across 11 displays. Ross Tessera and Carbonite run content on a 12G-SDI system. The field-level control room uses a GV K-Frame with a 3M/E Kayenne panel, Evertz NEXX routing and DreamCatcher replay, and LDX 150/135 cameras. Infrastructure is 3G-SDI baseband.
items.why: The team chose SDI at launch for I/O count and budget, but bought hybrid gear so IP can be added later by card or license in one to two years. It's a practical alternative to a full 2110 build on day one.

items.spec: Preset recall, live pan/tilt/zoom, tally; one or multiple Canon PTZs up to 4K

issues.headline: NAB NY opens with IP monitoring and control
issues.topline: NAB Show New York opens today at Javits with few big launches. The useful news is in the plumbing: Qligent makes ST 2110-capable compliance monitoring free at its base tier, and Arkona's BLADE//runner gets native Bitfocus Buttons control.

items.brief: Vision drops version-based licensing for tiered levels; the base compliance tier is now free.
items.price: Level 5 free; Levels 6/7 and multi-site aggregation priced separately (not published)
items.spec: Level 5: hardware ingest, ST 2110, SDI/ASI, ATSC 1.0/3.0; Level 6 AI root cause; Level 7 end-to-end observability
items.title: Vision monitoring levels (Level 5 free)
items.watch: Free-tier limits, paid-tier pricing and a general release date, none of which Qligent has published yet.
items.what: Qligent is replacing Vision software versions with tiered 'monitoring levels'. Level 5, aimed at single stations, costs nothing and its latest build adds hardware ingest, ST 2110 support and wider SDI/ASI transport support. Level 6 adds AI root-cause analysis and health reports, and Level 7 extends monitoring to the systems and networks behind the signal. It runs on-prem, in the cloud or hybrid.
items.why: A free ST 2110-aware compliance monitor lowers the cost of adding signal QC to a smaller IP plant or a single-site build. Check what the free tier actually caps before relying on it.

items.brief: Native Buttons module routes and monitors BLADE//runner blades from hardware panels; shipping now.
items.spec: arkona module v1.0.0; requires Buttons v1.8.2+; ST 2110 and SDI
items.title: BLADE//runner AT300 module for Bitfocus Buttons
items.watch: Whether the module adds processing-app control (beyond routing) in later versions.
items.what: Arkona released a native module (v1.0.0) for Bitfocus Buttons, available now in Buttons v1.8.2 and later. It routes SDI and audio signals between blades and to third-party devices, auto-discovers sources and destinations, and shows I/O lock, routing, PTP lock, PSU voltage, CPU and uptime. It can also identify and reboot blades and comes with preset templates.
items.why: Operators get a hardware panel for routing and health checks on AT300 blades without building a custom control layer, for both ST 2110 and SDI jobs.

items.brief: miriOS ships next week for X510; X610 adds more 5G, more Starlink and SRT-to-NDI hub.
items.spec: X510: OpenWrt + Speedify bonding; X610: more 5G modems, more Starlink inputs, faster wired, Broadcast Hub (SRT in → streaming/CDN/NDI out)
items.title: miriOS for X510, X610 bonding router preview
items.watch: X610 modem count, pricing and confirmed ship date.
items.what: Miri will demo the new miriOS on its X510 bonding router at Booth 147. miriOS adds a monitoring dashboard and multi-device remote management, and Miri says its public release is next week. It also previewed the X610, due early 2027, with more 5G modems, support for more Starlink units and a Broadcast Hub that turns incoming SRT feeds into streaming, CDN or NDI outputs.
items.why: A low-cost bonded-cellular and Starlink option for small REMI or event-streaming kits; the X610's SRT-to-NDI conversion could remove a separate gateway from the receive side.

items.brief: JPEG XS, IPMX and ST 2110 tools for COTS, including uncompressed ST 2110-20 in TitaniumViewer.
items.spec: SDK 2.0: JPEG XS, ST 2110, IPMX, NMOS, PTP, AES67 on COTS; TicoXS FIP HD/4K/8K with TDC; IPMX-certified Titanium FPGA SoC EDK
items.title: Titanium SDK 2.0, TitaniumViewer and TicoXS FIP
items.watch: Which OEM converters and LED processors ship with the TDC and IPMX cores.
items.what: intoPIX is showing Titanium SDK 2.0 for software senders and receivers on COTS hardware, and IPMX-certified Windows apps (TitaniumViewer, TitaniumShow) that turn a PC into an IPMX/ST 2110 endpoint. TitaniumViewer adds Privacy Encryption Protocol support and uncompressed HD over ST 2110-20. Also on show: TicoXS FPGA cores with Temporal Differential Coding, and TicoRAW Bayer transport over ST 2110 or RDMA.
items.why: A PC-based IPMX/2110 receiver is a cheap confidence monitor or graphics source on an IP show network. The FPGA cores also signal what JPEG XS features will turn up in vendors' converters.

items.title: ROE Visual Nashville hub
items.watch: Whether the hub holds rental-grade spares for current lines (e.g. Black Pearl, Carbon) and Academy course dates.
items.what: ROE Visual opened a Nashville hub offering LED repair, stock and ROE Academy training, which it pitches as closer to East Coast tours. An open house is set for Oct. 28. The report gives no address or size.
items.why: Local repair and spares can mean faster turnaround on damaged panels during a tour run than shipping to the West Coast.

items.brief: NEP Ceres and Mercury are the game units, with EVS replay run from Bristol and at-home operators.
items.title: ESPN NFL international games, London and Paris
items.watch: Any follow-up from ESPN on the transport, latency figures or switcher used.
items.what: ESPN is producing the October NFL games in London and Paris with NEP's OB trucks Ceres and Mercury as the main units. Coverage includes an aerial camera, live drone, pylon cameras, RF Steadicam and extensive super slow-mo. EVS replay resources run from ESPN's Bristol plant, with replay operators working from home in the US. The last game is Steelers vs. Saints at Stade de France on Oct. 25.
items.why: This is transatlantic split production with replay back in the US, at NFL scale. ESPN says it built transmission workflows specifically to cut latency, and the same model applies to any overseas event you want to run with a lighter crew on site.
